title: Universal recovery in approximate quantum error correction
abstract: Completes a theory of universal recovery for approximate QEC: a single recovery map corrects every channel controlled by a given error set. Approximate correctability is quantified by the environment-leakage distance (worst case) and the Knill-Laflamme Hellinger distance (average case); both control universal decoding. The Petz map associated with an error set is studied as an explicit universal recovery with uniform guarantees. Companion to arXiv:2607.22995.
key_claims: A single recovery map universally corrects all channels controlled by an error set in AQEC
Environment-leakage and Knill-Laflamme Hellinger distances control universal decoding
Petz map of the error set gives uniform average- and worst-case guarantees
relevance_note: Abstract only, NOT read. HYP-033-adjacent: HYP-033's recoverability observable descends from the decoupling / recoverability duality of PAPER-2026-143 as imported by PAPER-2026-142 (Kim-Kastoryano MERA). This paper gives general AQEC recovery guarantees in terms of leakage distances, which could turn a measured decoupling number into a recovery-error bound. It does not address networks, causal cones or minimal cuts, so it does not change the HYP-033 outcome count. Companion arXiv:2607.22995 not checked and not catalogued.
